newsitem.title: SWEDEN: AGA says new projects will lift margins.
newsitem.headline: AGA says new projects will lift margins.

text.p: Swedish medical and industrial gas group AGA AB said on Monday it expects new projects within the business area Process Industry to contribute to lifting operating margins in 1997 and 1998.
"When I look at these projects (21 projects 1993-1996), I distinctly see we will get an improvement in margins starting with 1997," AGA's president Lennart Selander told Reuters in an interview.
He pointed to that there are agreements over several years which regulate, among other things, prices and that each project has been carefully gone over customer by customer.
AGA has said that the operating margin would rise to 15 percent in 1999 at the latest from 12.2 percent in 1996.
"The improvement in the margin will be pretty equally divided over the years," Selander said.

New large plants often replace old small ones, which is one contributing factor to the improvement in profitability. This in turn lowers energy consumption by up to 50 percent, which is the largest single cost when producing airgas.
Concerning AGA's aim to every year increase its earnings per share, Selander believes downturns in the business trends of the gas sector can be compensated for as fluctuations are so small.
"AGA clearly reflects the fluctuations in the gas industry but we think they are so limited that profit per share should not have to fall," Selander said.
"This is an aim, which we think is realistic."
